---
title: "Precision and file sizes"
subtitle: "How the files are kept small, and what that means for the values in them"
aliases:
  - data_volume.html
---

FesmData puts many datasets on many grids, from 25 m to 5°. To keep the releases small
enough to download and store, the files are made only on the grids that need them, and
their values are rounded to a precision well below the uncertainty of the data. None of
this changes how the files are read: they are ordinary NetCDF-4 files with Float32 and
integer variables.

## Resolution

A thematic dataset (GHF, SMB, Velocity, ...) is made only on grids that add information:
as a rule, no grid is finer than about a quarter of the spacing of its source, e.g. 16 km
and 0.5° for sources at 1-2°, 8 km and 0.25° for sources at 0.25-0.5°, 4 km for most
others. A finer grid of a coarse source would only be large; a model that needs it can
remap online. Topo and Regions, made from high-resolution sources, are on all grids. The
nests and crops of a domain get the thematic datasets by cropping those of the domain
(see [Domains](domains.qmd#which-datasets-are-on-which-grids)).

## Precision

Each float field is rounded on output to a tolerance that depends on its kind, well
below the uncertainty of the data: the mantissa bits of each value that are not needed
for that tolerance are set to zero (bit rounding), which compresses much better. The
values stay Float32, and missing values are kept.

| Kind of field | Recognised by | Tolerance |
|---|---|---|
| Longitude, latitude (`lon2D`, `lat2D`) | name, or units `degrees_east`, `degrees_north` | lossless |
| Cell area (`area`) | name | 1e-5 relative (0.001%) |
| Fractions (`f_ice`, `f_valid`, cloud cover, albedo, ...) | name `f_*`, or units `1` | 0.001 |
| Ice velocities (`ux_srf`, `uy_srf`, `uxy_srf` and their errors) | name `ux`, `uy`, `uz`, `uxy`, and units `m yr-1` | 1% or 1 m yr-1, the larger |
| Rates (`smb`, `pr`, `sf`, `rf`, `melt`, `runoff`, `subl`, `bmelt`, ...) | name | 1% |
| Elevations, thicknesses, depths (`z_*`, `H_*`, their `*_sd`, ...) | units `m` | 0.01 m |
| Temperatures | units `K`, `degC` | 0.01 K |
| Other rates and fluxes (`dzdt`, winds, `ghf`, radiation, ...) | units per time (`yr-1`, `s-1`, `d-1`), or `W m-2` | 1% |
| Everything else (salinity, viscosity, ages, distances in km, ...) | | 3 significant digits (0.05%) |

The first row that matches a field applies. Integer fields (masks, classes, region
numbers) are never rounded. A relative tolerance holds for each value; for an absolute
tolerance, the bits kept are set by the largest magnitude of the field, so that every
value is within it; most errors are well below the tolerance. The coarser Topo grids and
the ensemble products are made from rounded files and rounded again, so their error can
exceed the tolerance slightly. The page of each dataset gives the precision of its
fields.

## Attributes

The precision of each field is in its attributes:

```
float z_bed(yc, xc) ;
        z_bed:units = "m" ;
        z_bed:precision = "0.01 m" ;
        z_bed:bitround_keepbits = 15 ;
```

`precision` is the tolerance (`"0.01 m"`, `"1%"`, `"1% or 1 m yr-1"`, `"lossless"`),
`bitround_keepbits` the mantissa bits kept (of 23; 23 is lossless).

## Compression

With the rounding, the fields are compressed with deflate level 4 (with shuffle). The
files are 1.4-1.5 times smaller than lossless files for Topo, and 2.4-4.6 times for
Regions and the thematic datasets (e.g. 3.3 for Velocity, 3.9 for SMB).

If a field needs a finer precision for your use, open an
[issue](https://github.com/fesmc/FesmData/issues).

## For maintainers

The tolerances are set in `shared/precision.jl`. A field that needs a finer precision (or
allows a coarser one) gets an exception in its product: `precision` in
`<Dataset>/remap.toml`, e.g. `precision = { ghf = 0.1, smb = "1%", lat = "lossless" }`
(see [Adding a dataset](adding.qmd#precision)). A domain may set another tolerance of
elevations and thicknesses (`elevation_precision` in `shared/domains.toml`); none does.
Intermediate files of the pipelines are not rounded.
